Empirical Research Plan:  Head Start and Life-Cycle Skill Formation (NLSY79 Child/YA)

-------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-------------------------------------------------
Primary strategy:  Fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity Design (FRD) that exploits the Federal Poverty Guideline (FPG) that determines Head Start eligibility.  
•  Eligibility rule: children in families with income ≤ 100 percent of the FPG (adjusted for family size) are entitled to a Head Start slot.  
•  Among families close to the cutoff, assignment is “as-good-as-random”; take-up is incomplete ⇒ FRD, where the poverty-rule indicator is used as an instrument for actual participation.  

Why RD is appropriate  
–  A sharp, well-publicised, nationwide threshold exists.  
–  The NLSY79 Child Supplement records pre-program family income, allowing precise construction of the running variable.  
–  Outcomes are measured years later, so no mechanical link to the running variable beyond the treatment.  
–  RD delivers local average treatment effects (LATE) for children whose participation status is altered by marginal eligibility—exactly the policy-relevant group for poverty-based targeting.

-------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
TREATi = 1 if child i ever attended Head Start at ages 3–4; 0 otherwise.

Instrument / Running variable  
RDi  = family incomei,age3  /  FPGfamily-size,year – 1  
Cutoff c = 0 (RDi ≤ 0 ⇒ eligible).  

FRD setup  
First-Stage:  TREATi = α1 + π ELIGi + f1(RDi) + ε1i  
Outcome:      Yi     = α2 + β TREATi  + g1(RDi) + ε2i  

Control group  
Children just above the cutoff (0 < RDi ≤ h) who are ineligible and have a low likelihood of participation.  
Bandwidth h chosen with MSE-optimal or robust bias-corrected selector (Calonico-Cattaneo-Titiunik).

Timing  
Income measured the calendar year in which the child is age 3 (baseline). Outcomes tracked up to early adulthood (18–30).  

-------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-------------------------------------------------
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes at c  
 Near the cutoff, untreated potential outcomes vary smoothly with family income.  
 Plausibility: parents cannot perfectly manipulate annual income to cross the FPG line; survey income is measured after the fact.

A2. First-stage relevance  
 Eligibility materially increases Head Start enrolment.  
 Plausibility: historical evidence shows large take-up discontinuity at 100 % FPG.

A3. No other discontinuous treatments at c  
 Other means-tested programs whose eligibility is keyed to the same FPG do not themselves drive later outcomes discontinuously (or can be controlled for).  
 Plausibility: many programs use the same cutoff; we will test for and control for contemporaneous participation.

A4. Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers) locally.  
 Within the narrow bandwidth, one child’s eligibility does not affect another child’s outcomes.

A5. Correct functional form / bandwidth choice  
 Local polynomials with robust bias-correction capture true conditional expectation around c.

-------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats & Mitigations
-------------------------------------------------
T1. Measurement error in baseline income → misclassification of eligibility  
 •  Use averaged income from two adjacent years (age 2–3 and age 3–4) to reduce noise.  
 •  Implement simulation-extrapolation (SIMEX) as a robustness check.

T2. Confounding means-tested programs at same cutoff  
 •  Control for contemporaneous participation in AFDC/TANF, Medicaid, SNAP recorded in NLSY.  
 •  Show RD plots for those programs to see if discontinuities explain outcomes.  
 •  Include multiple-treatment FRD in robustness section.

T3. Attrition / migration bias in long-run outcomes  
 •  Show McCrary-type density tests on sample retention around c.  
 •  Estimate bounds using Lee (2009) trimming if attrition is differential.  
 •  Weight by inverse-probability of remaining in sample.

-------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-------------------------------------------------
```r
########################################################
# 1. Load packages
########################################################
library(data.table)      # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)          # IV regressions & FE
library(rdrobust)        # RD estimation
library(rddensity)       # McCrary test

########################################################
# 2. Load and merge data (assume local CSVs)
########################################################
children  <- fread("nlsy79_child.csv")        # child-level info
families  <- fread("nlsy79_family.csv")       # family income etc.

dt <- merge(children, families, by = "child_id")

########################################################
# 3. Variable construction
########################################################
# Poverty guideline table assumed preloaded as 'fpg_table' with vars:
# year, family_size, fpg_dollars
dt <- merge(dt, fpg_table, 
            by.x = c("year_age3","family_size"), 
            by.y = c("year","family_size"), all.x = TRUE)

dt[, pov_ratio   := income_age3 / fpg_dollars]     # income to poverty
dt[, running_var := pov_ratio - 1]                # centered at cutoff
dt[, eligible    := as.integer(running_var <= 0)] # instrument

# Outcomes
dt[, testscore_std  := (testscore_age10 - mean(testscore_age10, na.rm=TRUE))/
                         sd(testscore_age10, na.rm=TRUE)]
dt[, hs_grad        := as.integer(hs_diploma == 1)]
dt[, log_earnings   := log(earnings_age25)]

########################################################
# 4. FRD – main specification (local linear, robust bias correction)
########################################################
# Example: standardized test score
main_rd <- rdrobust(y = dt$testscore_std,
                    x = dt$running_var,
                    fuzzy = dt$headstart,
                    c = 0,  p = 1, bwselect = "msetwo")

print(summary(main_rd))

########################################################
# 5. First-stage IV estimate (global polynomial, bandwidth h=0.5)
########################################################
bw <- 0.5
sub <- dt[abs(running_var) <= bw]

fs <- feols(headstart ~ eligible:poly(running_var,1) | 0,
            data = sub)
summary(fs)

########################################################
# 6. Robustness – different bandwidth & donut hole
########################################################
# Bandwidth sensitivity
for(h in c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6)){
  tmp <- dt[abs(running_var) <= h]
  res <- rdrobust(y = tmp$testscore_std,
                  x = tmp$running_var,
                  fuzzy = tmp$headstart)
  print(paste("Bandwidth",h,"ATE=", round(res$Estimate[1],3)))
}

# Donut RD: drop |running_var| < 0.02
donut <- dt[abs(running_var) > 0.02 & abs(running_var) <= 0.5]
donut_res <- rdrobust(y = donut$testscore_std,
                      x = donut$running_var,
                      fuzzy = donut$headstart)
print(summary(donut_res))
```

-------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-------------------------------------------------
Theory and prior quasi-experimental work (e.g., Deming 2009) suggest:  
•  Cognitive & non-cognitive skills: +0.10–0.20 SD by middle school.  
•  Educational attainment: +4–6 percentage-point increase in high-school graduation.  
•  Early-adult earnings: +6–8 percent (approx. 0.06–0.08 log points).  
We therefore expect β > 0 for test scores and educational outcomes and β ≈ 0.07 log points for earnings among compliers.

-------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RD)
-------------------------------------------------
C1. Density of running variable continuous at cutoff ….. 0.8  
 (McCrary test likely passes, but measurement error could blur.)  
C2. Covariates balanced locally …………………………………… 0.8  
 (We will test observable balance.)  
C3. No other discontinuous treatments …………………….. 0.5  
 (Potential contamination from Medicaid et al.; mitigations planned.)  
C4. Robust to bandwidth & polynomial choice …………… 0.9  
 (We run MSE-optimal, sensitivity & donut checks.)  
C5. Limited attrition / selective sample …………………… 0.7  
 (Attrition exists in NLSY; bounding exercises included.)

Average score: 0.74 → Generally credible but hinging on assumption about other means-tested programs and attrition.

-------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
